name: Trading on material non-public information (flagged: illegal, survey only)
one_line: Duty-holders (soldiers, engineers, speech staff, officers) buy known outcomes at longshot prices before the news; charged by the CFTC and SDNY in 2026; included only as the measurable adverse-selection counterparty of every maker and longshot seller in geopolitics, mentions, tech and culture markets.
maturity: Established practice (illegal): two CFTC/SDNY cases on polymarket.com trades reproduced on-chain to the dollar ($409,882 Maduro; ~$1.2M Year in Search), one $172k settlement, Israeli espionage indictments, ~$143M screened anomalous profit over two years; no lawful implementation exists and following it is unproven (file 27)
requires_ai: no; insiders used a browser or a bot (7 to a few thousand orders); the builder's exposure ledger is a nightly batch
edge: Misappropriated information; resting makers and NO holders at longshot prices pay
capital: none for the builder (a cost line); insiders staked $32.5k to $2.75M
build_time: 2-4 days for the exposure ledger on an existing stack
opportunity_size: ~$143M lower-bound anomalous profit Feb 2024-Feb 2026 (~$70M/yr); 152 military wallets $8M; shrinking under enforcement; for makers a 10.6%-of-Gamma-volume (25% of one-sided notional) loss in the Maduro tape
expected_results: Documented outcomes: $404k then indictment; ~$1.2M then criminal complaint; $172k paid back and 3-year ban; no lawful return series
competition: Copycat bots and whales, Polymarket ML surveillance, Chainalysis/Palantir, ACDC-style researchers
flag: prohibited: ToS §4.2 three prongs, Rule 7.2(g)-(i), CEA §6(c)(1), Reg 180.1
validate: Own-fill event study: pre-news losses vs gross income per family over 200+ resolved markets; >25% fails
top_risk: For the builder: pre-news adverse selection in fee-free geopolitics with no rebate offset
solo_fit_reason: Not a strategy anyone may run: criminal exposure, permanent on-chain trail, platform referrals and CFTC/SDNY action; its only use to a solo builder is as a measured cost input and a fingerprint set for file 27's quote-pull trigger.
speed_class: execution-sensitive: insiders trade minutes to days early; only the fill-to-cancel latency of the honest maker matters
results_1k: not workable (prohibited); honest-maker cost line only
results_5k: -$60 to -$320/month adverse-selection cost for a $5k geopolitics maker (guess, derived from two tapes)
results_10k: -$110 to -$620/month across geopolitics, mentions, tech, culture (guess)
min_capital: none; the ledger is free and the file is a cost, not a strategy
capacity_ceiling: longshot depth per market for insiders (1.28M shares below 0.35 in Maduro's last four days); cost scales with resting size for makers

Cite-check + skeptic pass 2026-09-28 (35 numbered sources re-fetched, 5 pack refs re-read, every own query re-run; one source added): Spagnuolo lane restated as 2,709 fills in 23 title-matched markets, 122 taker fills, 42% of lane notional resting (54% wallet-wide); Iran six-hour figures restated at the stated 0.35 cap (40 wallets, 1.40M shares, $263k, $1.14M seller loss); the Maduro '10.6% of volume' given its denominator (Gamma both-sides $10.97M; 25% of the $4.54M one-sided taker notional); Magamyman's Feb 27-28 sequence written out (sold Yes at 0.14-0.16 the afternoon before, re-bought $85.5k from 05:15:53, sold 190k back within 90 s, net ~250k shares / $53k new Yes in the hour) so the Harvard '$553k' and '71 minutes' narrative is contrasted with the tape; wallet-age classification completed for all top buyers via /activity ASC (Maduro 10 of 45, $21,985; Iran 10 of 40, $39,326, all created 00:50-05:56 UTC on strike day; OpenAI 10 of 45, $65,837) replacing the 'could not be classified' caveats; the second Maduro-cluster wallet from Nechepurenko's Table 3 (created 03:42 UTC on 3 Jan, $141,619.92) tied to the own recount; Perez identified as a Kalshi mention-market case (KalshiEX assisted); HN citation moved to the comment ids (48008935, 48009250) that carry the quotes; SSRN paper shown under two ids (7259741 DOI, 6426778 listing), both 403, so the $143M / 69.9% figures are sourced to the Forum post, Mitts' Columbia Law interview (new [36]) and the arXiv comparison; the unsupported 'Data API 800 req/10 s' replaced by E1's Gamma limits and the observed 429; /v2/user-pnl 'intermittently empty' note softened (answered every call today); v2 resolutions re-run on six markets: was_disputed true only on d4vd, false on the Venezuela market where Gamma records a dispute; $1k row now carries the honest-maker cost line; selection-bias caveat added to the loss-rate rows; 'a few dozen orders' corrected to the actual fill counts.
open_doubts: The $143M and 1,950-account figures come from screens with unknown precision; neither underlying account list is public, and the Mitts-Ofir paper text is still unread (SSRN 403 under both ids), so its figures rest on the authors' Forum summary, a Columbia Law interview and Nechepurenko's comparison paper.

Harvard Forum's 'six newly created wallets ~$1.2M' and 'Magamyman ~$553,000 / first trade 71 minutes before' do not reproduce on the Data API: Magamyman realised $195k on the Feb-28 rung ($808k lifetime, mostly Iran markets), had traded the rung since 16 February and reversed from No to Yes 58 minutes before the jump; the ten fresh wallets among the 40 largest pre-news buyers bought $39k, not $1.2M of profit; the paper may define the cluster differently.

The seller-loss figures assume the takers' counterparties held to resolution; some resting sellers were NO buyers via minting who may have hedged; the Iran figure counts only fills of at least $1,000; and both tapes are the largest charged cases, so the 10.6% / 25% loss rates are a ceiling, not an expectation.

Polymarket's referral counts (90+/100+, 315+ wallets, 2 arrests) are self-reported and unaudited; DOJ pages sit behind an interstitial challenge with no Wayback copy, so the parallel criminal cases are cited through the CFTC releases, the House Oversight release and the arXiv paper.
The Bubblemaps 93% trader, the New York Times '80+ users' figure and the Wikipedia-sourced Israeli figures ($244,000, $46,000, 'entire squadron') are known only through secondary or tertiary sources.
